newsitem.title: USA: USDA to release U.S. ag export forecast Thursday.
newsitem.headline: USDA to release U.S. ag export forecast Thursday.

text.p: The Agricultural Department is slated to release its first projection of U.S. agricultural exports in fiscal year 1997 on Thursday and the big question is whether exports will keep pace with 1996's record level.
USDA has pegged U.S. agricultural exports in fiscal year 1996 at a record $60 billion, driven by strong global demand for wheat and feedgrains coupled with high prices.
The department will also issue a revised forecast for fiscal year 1996 in the quarterly report, which will be released at 1500/1900 EDT.

Analysts expect U.S. exports to remain strong in 1997 with good demand for feedgrains, oilseeds and livestock, but note the outlook for wheat is uncertain as competitors like Argentina, Canada and Australia enter the market with increased supplies this year.
"I think the overall demand picture is likely to remain fairly strong," said Gary Adams, a crop analyst at the Food and Agricultural Policy Research Institute in Columbia, Mo.
"As we look at the longer term in our projections we do show as demand increases the U.S. should be in a position to expand exports," Adams added.

USDA will also be looking at whether growth in high value products will continue. High value exports surged by about 20 percent in 1996, surpassing growth in bulk exports and reversing a long-term trend.
The fiscal year runs from Oct. 1 through Sept 30.
The export report is released jointly by USDA's Economic Research Service, Foreign Agricultural Service, and the World Agricultural Board.
The Clinton administration has made boosting U.S. agricultural exports a top priority.
